_meta.note: Downloaded from Instagram's CDN, which serves short-lived URLs — these local copies are the durable version. Every `description` and `alt` was written after viewing the actual image, not inferred from the caption.
_meta.rights: All images were published by the organization on its own account. They are presumably theirs to reuse, but the ones showing identifiable people (`peopleVisible: true`) should be confirmed with the individuals before going on the website — Instagram consent is not website consent.

images.subject: Voices for Rare Advocacy Breakfast — group photo
images.description: Roughly 60–80 attendees posed on the grand staircase inside Queen's Park, under a large chandelier, with oil portraits on the walls. Most wear name badges. A child in a wheelchair sits at the front centre; one attendee holds a framed photograph. The full 'OntarioRare ACTION GROUP' logo is watermarked bottom-right.
images.alt: Attendees of the Ontario Rare Action Group's first Voices for Rare Advocacy Breakfast gathered on the staircase at Queen's Park.
images.suggestedUse: The single strongest asset on the account. Events page hero, or the home page featured-event card. Real, on-brand, and it visually substantiates the '80+ attendees' claim.

images.subject: Meet Pearl — story card
images.description: Cream card. 'Meet Pearl' in large outlined orange display type, the 'OntarioRare' wordmark beneath in purple, and a hand-drawn orange sun doodle top-right. A cut-out colour photograph of Pearl in a grey hoodie, hand to her head. Italic purple text reads 'Pearl lives with Cystic Fibrosis'.
images.alt: Pearl Cooley, who lives with cystic fibrosis.
images.suggestedUse: Story card image for content/stories.json → pearl-cooley.

images.subject: Meet Kristen — story card
images.description: Same template as Pearl's. 'Meet Kristen' outlined in orange, 'OntarioRare' wordmark, orange sun doodle. Black-and-white cut-out photograph of Kristen smiling in glasses and a Roots hoodie. Italic purple text: 'Kristen lives with Myelofibrosis'.
images.alt: Kristen Hummel, who lives with myelofibrosis.
images.suggestedUse: Story card image for content/stories.json → kristen-hummel.

images.subject: Spotlight Story — Sandra & Zach
images.description: Lavender background. 'SPOTLIGHT STORY' across the top in heavy white caps; 'SANDRA & ZACH' bottom-right. A cut-out photograph of Zach and his mother Sandra cheek to cheek, both smiling. Zach wears a black beanie embroidered 'CCC — Coalition to Cure CHD2'.
images.alt: Sandra Markus and her son Zach, who lives with a CHD2-related disorder.
images.suggestedUse: Story card image for content/stories.json → sandra-markus. Note this is a different template from the 'Meet X' cards — the account uses 'SPOTLIGHT STORY' for caregiver features.
images.note: Zach's beanie identifies the Coalition to Cure CHD2 — see organizations.json.

images.subject: Connecting Patients to Care — five-stage framework
images.description: White/purple infographic. Heading 'Connecting Patients to Care' with a heart divider and the line 'Every rare disease journey deserves timely diagnosis, treatment access, research, and support.' A heartbeat line links five purple line-icons: family, DNA helix, microscope, IV bag, and a heart containing figures — labelled FAMILY, DIAGNOSIS, RESEARCH, TREATMENT, HOPE & COMMUNITY. Along the bottom, seven people of varying ages seen from behind, mostly in purple, one using a wheelchair.
images.alt: Infographic showing the five stages of connecting rare disease patients to care: family, diagnosis, research, treatment, and hope and community.
images.suggestedUse: Important — this is a real framework the organization uses. Could restructure the Advocacy page around these five stages instead of the six invented commitments. See advocacyFramework in events.json.

images.subject: June 16 meeting announcement
images.description: Pale lavender card with a faint DNA-helix watermark. 'Join us June 16th at 7:00pm ET' in purple, 'Via Zoom' beneath, then a June 2026 calendar grid with the 16th hand-circled. Full 'OntarioRare ACTION GROUP' lockup at the bottom.
images.alt: Announcement for the Ontario Rare Action Group meeting on June 16, 2026 at 7pm ET via Zoom.
images.suggestedUse: Confirms the June 16 meeting was held **via Zoom** — a detail the caption omits. Template worth reusing for future event announcements.

images.subject: Rare Disease Organizations — Join Us
images.description: Pale lavender card with layered crescent shapes. A circular photo crop, shot from below, of six or seven hands of varying skin tones stacked together in a team huddle. Text: 'Rare Disease Organizations' in black, 'JOIN US' in bold purple caps. 'OntarioRare' wordmark bottom-right.
images.alt: Hands stacked together above an invitation for rare disease organizations to join.
images.suggestedUse: Partners page — pairs with the recruitment copy in organizations.json.

images.subject: Summer Outreach Starts Now
images.description: Cream card. 'Summer Outreach' in large outlined orange display type with 'STARTS NOW' solid beneath, an orange sun doodle top-right, and a crayon-textured illustration of a hand holding a megaphone in yellow, pink, teal and orange. A teal circular arrow button suggests swiping. 'OntarioRare' wordmark bottom-left.
images.alt: Illustration of a hand holding a megaphone, announcing that summer outreach starts now.
images.suggestedUse: Advocacy page — the MPP outreach campaign section.

images.subject: Summer MPP outreach — the ask
images.description: Cream card, orange bold text only: 'Connect with your local MPP this summer—whether at their constituency office or at community events—to build meaningful relationships and increase understanding of rare disease issues.'
images.alt: Text encouraging supporters to connect with their local MPP over the summer.
images.suggestedUse: The copy itself is more useful than the image — already captured in events.json → campaigns.

images.subject: Happy Canada Day
images.description: Photograph, cropped to a dome, of a Canadian flag flying beside an ornate Romanesque sandstone building with arched windows — Old City Hall / Queen's Park style architecture. Below on pale lavender: 'HAPPY CANADA DAY / BONNE FÊTE DU CANADA' over a faint maple leaf. 'OntarioRare' wordmark bottom-right.
images.alt: A Canadian flag flying beside a historic sandstone building, with Canada Day greetings.
images.suggestedUse: Seasonal — limited website use.

images.subject: Ontario, we can do better than this
images.description: Video title frame: a warmly lit photograph of a woman embracing a child outdoors, overlaid with the purple 'OntarioRare ACTION GROUP' logo and a large translucent 'OR' monogram.
images.alt: A woman embracing a child outdoors, with the Ontario Rare Action Group logo.

images.subject: this is rare
images.description: Black-and-white video frame: a woman on the floor of a living room laughing with several young children climbing on and hugging her. Lowercase caption overlay reads 'this is rare'.
images.alt: A black-and-white photo of a woman laughing with several young children, captioned 'this is rare'.
images.suggestedUse: Videos page thumbnail. The 'this is rare' framing is strong — reusable as a section heading.

images.subject: Account avatar / logo
images.description: The 'OntarioRare ACTION GROUP' logo in white over a deep purple gradient, with a large 'OR' monogram behind it, filled with faint photographic imagery.
images.alt: Ontario Rare Action Group logo.
images.suggestedUse: Reference only — the repo already has public/OntarioRare_Logo.png and public/logo.png at better resolution. Useful for confirming the official lockup: 'OntarioRare' with 'ACTION GROUP' beneath.

images.subject: Hallelujah series 1 of 7
images.description: Casual selfie-style photograph of a young woman on a sofa holding a floral mug, with a lavender text box overlaid reading: “Treatment access without entering your villain era… hallelujah”
images.alt: A young advocate holding a mug, with the caption: Treatment access without entering your villain era… hallelujah
images.suggestedUse: The overlay copy is the valuable part — seven policy pain points phrased as wishes. Excellent raw material for the Challenges page. The photos themselves are informal and off-brand for the website.
images.warning: The person shown is not named in the post and I did not identify her. Do not publish her image without confirming who she is and getting consent.
